scholarships.title: First Nations Cancer Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Postgraduate Certificate, Master's, PhD, Honours, Graduate Certificate, Research Postdoctoral

eligibility: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander student only
Undertaking full-time postgraduate study or research in a cancer-related field in health, research or policy
Postgraduate study or research at a recognised university or institute in Australia, the United States or the United Kingdom
Graduate student, health professional or early-career researcher
Must be able to demonstrate how the study or research will improve cancer-related outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students only, undertaking full-time postgraduate study or research in a cancer-related field in health, research or policy, at a full-time study load. Applicants must demonstrate how their study or research will affect Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in improving cancer-related outcomes.
benefits: Up to AUD 120,000 per year for up to three years as a contribution towards the cost of full-time postgraduate study or research
Accommodation and travel expenses related to research, fieldwork or conferences
Textbooks and other essential study-related equipment
Living expenses such as accommodation, transportation, food and other dietary requirements
Access to academic, health and wellbeing services
Up to AUD 5,000 per year in tailored academic and wellbeing support

requirements: Must be undertaking full-time postgraduate study or research
Scholarship funds cannot be used for study or research expenses that should be covered by the university or institute
application_method: Read the Scholarship Guidelines linked from the Aurora scholarship page to confirm eligibility criteria and required documents
Apply through Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal
Optionally contact the Aurora Pathways Scholarship team before applying to discuss the application
existing.selection_notes: Applicants are assessed on their ability to demonstrate how their study or research will impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in improving cancer-related outcomes. Aurora states the programme exists because cancer is the leading cause of death among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people while fewer than one per cent of health professionals identify as Indigenous, and that scholars are drawn from all walks of life but share a commitment to improving outcomes for their own communities.
existing.best_fit: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander graduate students, health professionals or early-career researchers already committed to full-time postgraduate study or research in cancer control, health, research or policy, at a recognised institution in Australia, the United States or the United Kingdom.
existing.notes: The scholarship covers study or research at institutions in Australia, the United States or the United Kingdom, so it is not restricted to Australian universities. Aurora's own page states that up to four scholarships will be awarded yearly from 2024 to 2026, which means continuation beyond 2026 is not confirmed by the awarding body; the Indigenous Pathways Portal showed the 2026 round as closed on 4 October 2026 with no 2027 window published.
existing.duration: Up to three years, with no need to re-apply each year once awarded
existing.application_period: The 2026 round opened 16 June 2026 and closed 11 September 2026. No 2027 window is published. Aurora states up to four scholarships are awarded yearly from 2024 to 2026.
existing.program_type: Charitable foundation and government co-funded research scholarship (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander graduate students)
